title: Oto-Manguean languages - Wikipedia
text: The Mixtec language is a complex set of regional varieties, many of which are not mutually intelligible. The varieties are sometimes grouped by geographic area by using designations such as those of the Mixteca Alta, the Mixteca Baja, and the Mixteca de la Costa.

title: Mixtec, Magdalena Peñasco Language (XTM) – L1 & L2 Speakers ...
text: Magdalena Peñasco Mixtec is an endangered indigenous language of Mexico. It belongs to the Otomanguean language family. The language is used as a first language by all adults in the ethnic community, but not all young people. It is not known to be taught in schools.

title: Mixtecan Family | SIL Mexico
text: The most famous collection of Mixtec artifacts was found in tomb seven at the Monte Alban archaeological site in Oaxaca. Like other Otomanguean languages, the languages in the Mixtecan family are tonal, which means that the pitch with which a word is pronounced is so important that a change in the pitch can change one word into an entirely different one.

title: Mixtec of Magdalena Peñasco | SIL Mexico
text: This language is also known as Sa'an Ñuu Savi, which means “Language of the Rain People”. The traditional territory in which this variety is spoken is the municipality of Magdalena Peñasco, which is located in the district of Tlaxiaco and to the east of the city, along the highway to Chalcatongo. In the neighboring municipalities of San Cristóbal Amoltepec, San Agustín Tlacotepec, and San Mateo Peñasco, variants of Mixtec are spoken that are similar to the variant spoken in Magdalena, and which are grouped under the same ISO code [xtm], but which have important differences.

text: January 17, 2026 - Aspect is primarily binary, distinguishing completive (perfective) from incompletive (imperfective) forms, with completive often marked by prefixes such as ni- or nu- that indicate completed actions, typically in the past. For instance, in many dialects, the completive form involves prefixes such as ni- or nu-, as in ni-jìnù 'I ran' (completed) in Magdalena Peñasco Mixtec, while the incompletive jínù means 'I run' (ongoing or habitual).
